system: You are a helpful assistant. Notes and summaries can drift from what they summarise. Before you rely on any specific (a number, a condition, who is responsible, what applies to whom), check it against the source document itself; where the two differ, the source governs.
message:

The coach leaves the main car park at 08:00 (arrive by 07:30) and returns around 16:30 on Friday. Activities — gorge walking, canoeing, climbing, orienteering and a night walk — are led by centre instructors with school staff supervising. Students may bring mobile phones, but they will be collected each night; staff will also post daily updates on the trip blog and the centre office takes emergency calls. Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
CASTLEFIELD ACADEMY — YEAR 8 RESIDENTIAL TRIP TO PEN-Y-GARREG OUTDOOR CENTRE Letter to parents and carers, 1 December 2026

Dear Parent/Carer,

We are delighted to offer all Year 8 students the opportunity to take part in our three-day residential trip to Pen-y-Garreg Outdoor Education Centre in the Brecon Beacons, from Wednesday 10 March to Friday 12 March 2027.

Itinerary. The coach will leave from the school's main car park at 08:00 on Wednesday 10 March; students must arrive by 07:30 for registration. We will return to the school at approximately 16:30 on Friday 12 March. Activities include gorge walking, canoeing, climbing, orienteering and a night walk. All activities are led by the centre's qualified instructors, with Castlefield staff supervising at all times.

Cost and payment. The total cost is £185 per student, covering coach travel, accommodation, all meals, activities, equipment hire and travel insurance. A non-refundable deposit of £50 is due by Friday 8 January 2027, with the balance of £135 due by Friday 12 February 2027. Payments should be made through ParentPay; instalments are welcome.

Financial support. Students who are eligible for the pupil premium will have 50% of the cost paid by the school. If your child is not eligible for the pupil premium and you are experiencing financial difficulty, please contact Mr Patel, Head of Year 8, in confidence; we will try to help, but we cannot guarantee support for all families.

Insurance. Travel and activity insurance is arranged by the school through the local authority's scheme and is included in the cost. You do not need to arrange separate insurance, although you may wish to check any personal possessions cover on your home insurance.

Medical needs and medication. Please complete the enclosed medical and consent form. All medication, including over-the-counter medicines, must be handed in a labelled bag to the trip leader, Mrs Lowe, at registration; she will look after it and supervise doses. The only exceptions are asthma inhalers and adrenaline auto-injectors, which students must carry themselves at all times.

Mobile phones and valuables. Students may not bring mobile phones, tablets or other electronic devices on this trip. This allows students to engage fully with the activities and with each other. Staff will post daily updates and photographs on the school's trip blog, and parents can contact the centre's office in an emergency on 01874 555 019. Any device found will be confiscated and returned on arrival back at school.

Kit. A kit list is enclosed. Students will need old trainers that can get wet, waterproofs, and warm layers. Pocket money of up to £15 is optional, for the centre's tuck shop.

Behaviour. Students are expected to follow the school's behaviour policy throughout. Serious misbehaviour may result in a student being sent home at the parents' expense.

Please return the consent form and pay the deposit by 8 January 2027. Places are limited to 90 students and will be allocated in order of receipt of deposits.

Yours faithfully, Mrs R. Lowe, Trip Leader and Head of PE
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. Do I need to buy travel insurance for my son for this trip?
2. We're not pupil premium but money is very tight this winter. If I contact Mr Patel, will the school definitely pay half?
3. What time must students arrive on the departure morning?
4. Can my daughter take her phone if she agrees to hand it in at night?
response:
I checked these against the letter itself, and my earlier notes were wrong on three of the four points. The answers below follow the letter.

**1. Do I need to buy travel insurance?**
No. Travel and activity insurance is included in the £185 and arranged by the school through the local authority's scheme. You don't need separate cover, though the letter suggests checking whether your home insurance covers personal possessions. *(My notes wrongly said parents should arrange their own.)*

**2. Will the school definitely pay half if I contact Mr Patel?**
No, it isn't guaranteed. The automatic 50% contribution is only for pupil premium students. For other families in financial difficulty, the letter says to contact Mr Patel, Head of Year 8, in confidence, and that the school "will try to help, but we cannot guarantee support for all families." It doesn't promise any particular amount. It's still worth contacting him soon, and instalments through ParentPay are also welcome. *(My notes wrongly said the 50% applied to these families too.)*

**3. What time must students arrive on departure morning?**
By **07:30** on Wednesday 10 March 2027, in the school's main car park, for registration. The coach leaves at 08:00.

**4. Can my daughter take her phone if she hands it in at night?**
No. Students may not bring mobile phones, tablets or any other electronic devices. Any device found will be confiscated and returned when the coach gets back to school. Instead, staff will post daily updates and photos on the school's trip blog, and in an emergency you can call the centre's office on **01874 555 019**. *(My notes wrongly said phones were allowed and collected each night.)*

Remember to return the consent form and pay the £50 deposit by **8 January 2027**. Places are limited to 90 and go in the order deposits are received.
